subject: science
passage: On Earth, nearly all the oxygen in the atmosphere is produced by photosynthesis; without living things to replenish it, oxygen would react with rocks and volcanic gases and largely disappear. Astrobiologist Mireille Fontaine therefore argues that if telescopes detect abundant oxygen in the atmosphere of an Earth-sized planet orbiting another star, astronomers will have found strong evidence of life.
passage_b: Oxygen's link to life on Earth is not a law of nature. On a planet orbiting a small, active red dwarf star, intense ultraviolet light could split water molecules high in the atmosphere; the light hydrogen would escape to space, leaving oxygen behind, possibly in large amounts, on a world with no life at all. Oxygen would become persuasive only alongside other clues, such as methane, a gas that reacts with oxygen and should soon vanish unless something keeps replenishing both.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument made by Fontaine in Text 1?

choices.A: By rejecting the claim that photosynthesis produces nearly all of Earth's atmospheric oxygen
choices.B: By claiming that methane, rather than oxygen, is the most reliable single sign of life
choices.C: By suggesting that planets orbiting red dwarf stars are unlikely to keep their atmospheres
choices.D: By arguing that oxygen on its own could mislead, since it might build up without any life

explanation.why: Fontaine treats abundant oxygen by itself as strong evidence of life. Text 2 describes how oxygen could accumulate "on a world with no life at all" and says oxygen "would become persuasive only alongside other clues." Text 2 would therefore say oxygen alone is not enough.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 speaks of "Oxygen's link to life on Earth" and does not dispute it; it denies only that the link must hold elsewhere.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 values methane only together with oxygen; it does not call methane by itself the most reliable sign.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2's red dwarf planet keeps its oxygen; nothing suggests such planets lose their atmospheres.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 shows how a lifeless planet could build up oxygen, so oxygen without other clues would not be strong evidence of life.
